Subject: Post-call: deployment path clarification (Hosted vs Dedicated)

Hi Peter — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposal for next steps so your team can decide on Hosted vs Dedicated capacity: 

Recap of requirements you shared
- Target p99 latency for inference: 60 ms (goal: 50 ms)
- Typical peak concurrent QPS: 180–220 on weekday evenings; spike tolerance up to ~350 for promotions
- Model: open-checkpoint LLM (13B baseline, expect to test quantized 8-bit variant)
- Data residency: US-only; no on-prem requirement at this stage

Initial recommendation (based on the call)
- Start on Redwood Hosted API with a Reserved Throughput plan: gives you immediate ability to scale, streaming responses, and built-in autoscaling policies. Hosted is the fastest to get started and lets us profile real traffic.
- If sustained peak QPS > 300 for multiple days or if p99 consistently < 45 ms is required, plan a migration to Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) to guarantee throughput and latency SLOs.

Key technical notes needed from Acuity to finalize config
1) A small sample of production request traces (anonymized) or a 24–72 hour replay of traffic so we can simulate batching and KV cache hit rates.
2) Expected average prompt + response token lengths (helps model selection and kernel choices).
3) Any specific adapter or retrieval latency that must be considered in the end-to-end SLO.

Proposed next steps
- I’ll attach a one-pager that contrasts Hosted vs Dedicated (quick reading).
- Can you share the sample workload (or let us run a short replay) by EOD Wednesday 11/25? That lets our infra team run a throughput/latency projection.
- If you’re comfortable, we can provision a 14-day Hosted trial with a small reserved throughput buffer and include a stove-top perf run (no charge) to collect perf numbers.

Attachments: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-onepager.pdf, acuity-performance-template.csv

Thanks — I’ll loop Marcus on the technical follow-up. Happy to hop on another 30m with your infra folks.

—

Peter / Kimberly — putting a short technical note here so we can converge: 

- Hosted autoscaling behavior: Hosted uses workload-aware continuous batching and autoscaling with a warm pool. For sudden drops (350 -> 50 QPS) we avoid aggressive scale-down for ~3–5 minutes to prevent queuing. Typical user-observed queuing is low unless backpressure hits GPU synchronous limits. For your pattern, we recommend a modest reserved buffer (~25% of your peak spike) during promotions.

- KV caching: Redwood supports prefix and KV cache across request streams. If your retrieval matcher is 60ms, we generally place retrieval before model invocation; the runtime can co-locate KV cache hits and serve from GPU memory. Cache consistency is per-deployment and configurable (eviction TTLs). No fundamental incompatibility here.

- Dedicated sizing (if you opt to move): for a 13B quantized model with 220 sustained QPS targeting p99 ~50–60ms, a conservative Dedicated starting point is 2 x A100-like GPUs with dedicated batch steering; for sustained >300 QPS consider 3 GPUs or sharding across a small pool. We should profile your real traces to refine these numbers — the numbers shift with token length and beam/streaming usage.

Links:
- Perf calculator: https://drive.redwood.com/perf-calc
- Hosted vs Dedicated playbook: https://drive.redwood.com/hosted-dedicated-playbook
